A "reserve drill" is a period of required training and duty for members of the military reserves or National Guard in the U.S. and other countries, officially called Inactive Duty for Training (IDT).

  • It typically consists of one weekend per month (often four 4-hour drill periods) and two weeks of Annual Training (AT) per year.
  • This part-time commitment allows reservists to maintain military readiness while pursuing civilian careers or education.
